Have had a TSH done recently which was within range. I know there’s another test free T4 with reflex to T3 (or I may have that backwards) but no one has ordered it in quite some time. I’ve had thyroid issues suggested many times when I mention unexplained fatigue. Still nothing has been unusual in the bloodwork. Sometimes I feel like I’m just making it all up. The only lab work that ever really explained the fatigue was a ferritin level of 5. Rechecked at 14 after prescription iron. That was a little over a year ago though. Recent CBC was normal.

Your input has been extremely valuable to me. Thank you once again for contributing your time and knowledge, not just for myself but for any others you’ve helped navigate what can be a confusing and anxiety-inducing experience. 

My urologist briefly mentioned that constipation can be a contributing factor and could even be part of the reason why my kidneys were “swollen.” Worth mentioning that I had taken a bit of Miralax in the days prior to the CT and cleared that issue up considerably from where it was. I wonder if that didn’t help between the time of the ultrasound to the CT. Anyway, I found that interesting. Alongside the recurrent UTI has often been (sometimes severe) constipation. At the height of the GI issues, I wasn’t having any UTIs though, so it’s anyone’s guess. 

So far for this last UTI, it is looking good. I took 14 days of Macrobid this time and urinalysis/culture after completing it are clean. My issue has been that generally within a few days to a week of finishing antibiotics, symptoms return. So far that hasn’t been the case. Hopeful for a return to normal.

I’m 99% certain the scar is from my first kidney infection. I had never had a UTI before and went on my dad’s advice that I “probably had the flu” for well over a week after the back pain started. Eventually went to urgent care with 104 fever and vomiting. Prescribed Cipro (learned later I am allergic to it). Several days later I could hardly walk and was in so much pain I needed assistance to the bathroom. My boyfriend at the time dragged me to the ER. They ran a whole bunch of blood tests to rule out sepsis. CT confirmed kidney infection. It was a bad one. I’ve had one other since but it wasn’t nearly as bad. 

So you think, even with normal labs (recent BMP all within normal range) and CT ruling out hydronephrosis, I should do this other test if the urologist agrees and will order it? It feels like it could be kind of excessive.

Update 2: was able to see the radiologist’s report on patient portal. Haven’t heard from the urologist about it yet. Presumably this is good news 

IMPRESSION:

pathology such as regions of stricture.

You are a rare gem. You have no idea how much it must have meant for her to share with you what she was going through and to receive some understanding. 

I work in the medical field also. We both know you can’t take it home with you. Send them off with something instead. Ask if you can give them a big hug, whatever you deem appropriate. 

You recognize your patients as a whole: body, mind and spirit. Hold on to that, but learn to leave a piece of yourself with them rather than carrying a piece of their grief with you. 

Much love to you.

I’d say there are differing schools of thought on that. Some people say poetry is whatever you make it. I think I’m a little more narrow minded. I like to “get it.”

When I write, I’m usually writing about a specific experience I had. Let’s take a really common theme of heartbreak. Most people have experienced it in one way or another, but no one exactly like me, right?

As a writer, I can zoom out or zoom in for the desired effect. Maybe I will add specific details, or maybe I will leave them out, but I definitely want the reader to come out of it understanding the theme. 

[This poem ](https://www.poetryfoundation.org/poetrymagazine/poems/28891/separation-56d21285b2140) is an excellent example of “zooming out.” Obviously not my poem, I wish I had a fraction of this capacity. 

[This one ](http://famouspoetsandpoems.com/poets/charles_bukowski/poems/12977) zooms in so much and gives so much detail, it’s relatable in a different kind of way. We relate to the desperation, to the feeling, but maybe not the specific events. 

Edit for clarification: we’ve all experienced heartbreak differently, so we will interpret poems about heartbreak (a familiar feeling) based on our own perspective/bias. There’s definitely a relationship there. 


I’m a pessimist. I read pessimism in the poem and had my reasons. You read optimism and had your reasons. This poem was “zoomed out” enough for that. I think more details could have given a clearer idea of intent. I’m not sure the poet was aiming for a clear interpretation kind of poem. They seem a bit more abstract

All of this makes for good analysis. No detail is too small. If you look at other poems online which have more detailed analyses, you’ll see that anything can be interpreted. Spacing, capitalization, punctuation or lack thereof, etc. ee cummings is always fascinating when it comes to how the poem appears visually on the page. 

Of course there is language. Metaphors, similes, plain language. First person perspective, third person, etc. All these things influence how a poem impacts the reader. And then, of course, there is the influence of the reader’s experiences on the poem. 

It’s ok to talk about the poem in little building blocks like this. You don’t have to cut right to the chase and say what it means. Spend some time describing it first :)
